description: You are a site reliability engineer tasked with monitoring uptime and ensuring secure handling of log files, which are currently vulnerable to unauthorized access due to world-readable permissions. There is an uptime log located at /home/user/logs/uptime.log containing historical uptime data. Your job is to fix the security vulnerability by changing the permissions so only the user (owner) can read and write to /home/user/logs/uptime.log, but no other users can access it. After you complete the permission fix, append a new log entry to /home/user/logs/uptime.log in the following precise format: Log entry format (single line, no additional text or spaces beyond required): YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS - uptime: UPTIME_VALUE Where: - YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS is the current date and time in 24-hour format (e.g., 2024-06-10 14:23:12) - UPTIME_VALUE is the output of the uptime -p command (e.g., "up 3 hours, 22 minutes") After completing, verify that the log file has rw------- permissions and contains the appended entry in the specified format. No other output is required.
truth:
Before the task begins:
- The directory /home/user/logs/ exists and is writable by user.
- The file /home/user/logs/uptime.log exists and is owned by user, with permissions 0644 (-rw-r--r--) and contains sample historical uptime data as follows (example):
2024-06-10 10:00:01 - uptime: up 2 hours, 12 minutes
2024-06-10 12:30:01 - uptime: up 4 hours, 42 minutes

After task completion:
- File /home/user/logs/uptime.log exists, owned by user, with permissions 0600 (-rw-------).
- The file's contents contain the previous lines, and a new appended entry as:
2024-06-10 14:23:12 - uptime: up 6 hours, 34 minutes

The timestamp and uptime value will reflect the actual time and system uptime when the agent appends the entry, but the format must be precisely:
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS - uptime: UPTIME_VALUE

Automated test will check:
- file permissions of /home/user/logs/uptime.log are 0600 (--rw-------)
- the file contains a single new log entry in the correct format at the end, matching current date/time and output of uptime -p.
